_comment: The block manifest consumed by `klt signoff --manifest` (klayout-tools
issue #722, Phase 0 of epic #706). This is the file the fleet tier
roll-up (2AMLogic/2am#956) consumes to grade this block's T1 state
mechanically, replacing the hand-maintained checkbox list on issue #3
-- see the `## The verdict of record` section there and issue #155 for
the contract.
block             required. Identifies this block's row in the fleet
roll-up, which consumes exactly this value.
kind              required. `mixed-signal`, confirmed against this
block rather than taken from issue #155: the TRNG
partitions into an analog entropy source plus
digitizer bank (design/sampler_core.spice's
`.subckt sampler_core`, laid out as
layout/sampler_core/sampler_core.gds) and a
digital conditioner/health section
(digital/rtl/trng_digital.v, synthesized in
digital/flow/). The partition boundary is stated
explicitly on issue #3 and in signoff/README.md;
the mixed-signal claim makes both columns of the
per-kind items (1, 2, 5, 7, 11) apply, once per
partition.
evidence          item id -> evidence entry. Partition-qualified
keys (`<id>.<analog|digital>`, klayout-tools
signoff's _lookup_evidence prefers them) are used
deliberately: a kind-independent item is graded
only for the partition whose evidence actually
backs it, so `3.analog` does not paint a `met` on
the digital partition, which has no layout at all
yet (no GDS exists to DRC or LVS).
What is deliberately NOT cited, item by item, against the current
tree (2026-09-21, @ origin/main):
1, 2, 9, 10       no klt verb backs these (klt signoff grades them on
'some passing envelope was cited', not topical
relevance); citing an unrelated passing envelope to
make the row go green is exactly what this manifest
exists to prevent. They render unmet/no_evidence.
5.analog           no `klt sim` envelope exists -- sim/ campaigns are
minted evidence records (sim/bin/evidence_record.py
shape), not `klt sim` output.
5.digital           no `klt sta` / SDF-annotated `klt
functional-verification` run exists.
6                  no `klt yield` report exists.
7.analog           no `klt pex` report exists -- post-layout
campaigns run from `klt extract --parasitics`
netlists via sim/bin harnesses, which item 7 by
design does not accept (a clean DRC or
pre-layout sim proves nothing post-layout).
7.digital           no post-route gate netlist exists yet.
8                  no aggregated, current characterization artifact
exists yet; a hand-rolled `"kind": "generic"`
wrapper asserting status pass would be a
self-attestation, not evidence.
11                 the item-11 `klt erc` supply evidence exists AND is
now cited (issue #161): `erc-supply-spec.json`
declares `ties[]` for every distinct well/substrate
tie this block draws -- 70 merged nwell regions to
vdd, 5 each to vddr1..vddr4, and the substrate to vss
-- graded `erc_status: clean` with zero findings and
a non-empty `erc_coverage.checked` (all six ties,
also listed in `checked_by_well_assertion`: the
per-supply well regions are asserted boxes derived
from the drawn nwell, because 0.6.0 checks every
merged polygon of a whole drawn well layer against
one net and this block's wells tie to five different
supplies) and nothing in `skipped` (sky130's tap is a
dedicated layer, so no tie is degenerate). The erc
citation is pinned to the envelope's
provenance.input.content_hash -- the committed
GDS's sha, same pin value as item 3; the SPEC's own
hash rides in the envelope's
provenance.spec.content_hash. The row still renders
`unmet`, for a reason that is now the LVS half
alone: `lvs_supply_unproven`. The grader's
no-PDN branch requires every declared supply to
appear in the cited lvs.json's
net_correspondence as a row whose ENTIRE
layout-side string equals that supply name -- but
klt lvs joins a label-merged net's aliases with
'|', so this block's six supply rows read
'G_VDDR_M1|...|VDDR|VDDR1' etc. and can never
equal 'vddr1' (no single-name supply row exists:
checked, 0 of 152). No spec-side name fixes both
halves at once (the ERC half needs real label
names; the LVS half needs exact alias-string
equality), so the citation is filed as the honest
mechanical verdict and the alias-joined-rows
pairing gap is filed upstream (friction protocol;
see signoff/README.md's item-11 section for the
issue link and the local follow-up). The
digital column stays uncited: item 11's
digital branch needs a place-and-route PDN
response plus a power_connectivity match,
and the digital partition has no layout at
all (same state as every other
partition-qualified row above).
Freshness pinning (`content_hash`): pinned wherever the cited
envelope's own shape records one. `layout/sampler_core/drc.json`
records provenance.input.content_hash, so item 3 is pinned to it;
that value is sha256 of the committed sampler_core.gds (verified
2026-09-21), so a regenerated DRC against a changed GDS no longer
matches the pin and renders the item stale -- the manifest rots
loudly, not silently. `layout/sampler_core/lvs.json` is a klt 0.4.0
envelope whose provenance carries no input.content_hash (its
freshness is recorded as environment.layout_sha256/reference_sha256
inside the envelope instead), and a manifest pin with no envelope
hash to match renders the citation stale_evidence -- so item 4 is
file-backed with NO pin, the one citation that cannot be pinned
today. signoff/README.md states the freshness verification that was
performed by hand for that row and why it cannot be mechanical yet
(the upstream fix is klayout-tools#2212, `verify a citation's
input against the artifact, not just the envelope`).
Regenerate the committed report (signoff/t1-report.json) with the
exact command in signoff/README.md -- the report embeds the
--tiers-doc label verbatim, so the invocation must match byte for
byte. CI re-runs the same command and diffs, so this file cannot
cite a changed artifact without going red (issue #155, `CI re-runs
it`).
